framework_reference_decision: No web framework detected. Per WORKFLOW.md 4.2.3, source/sink shapes were derived from repository code using the Python language reference only; assumptions recorded in this file.

extraction_scope.included: python/paddle/% (the shipped framework package: distributed launch/fleet/elastic tooling, utils, base, incubate, hapi)
excluded: tools/% (CI/build automation scripts, not shipped with the wheel)

extraction_query_metadata.reason: These are raw BQRS extraction queries for 'codeql query run' + 'codeql bqrs decode' with a multi-column select. '@kind problem' is wrong for multi-column candidate rows and no '@kind table' exists for this purpose, so no @kind is annotated. SARIF-oriented metadata (@kind path-problem, @problem.severity error) is only used later for the Pass 2 taint query.
csv_columns: node (AST element; decodes to file:line in BQRS)

assumptions: Paddle is a library/CLI framework, not a web service: the attacker-relevant input boundary is the process environment of the machine running Paddle - CLI arguments and training_script_args of 'python -m paddle.distributed.launch'/'fleet launch', environment variables (PADDLE_* cluster topology), JSON config files, socket/etcd peer data, and download URLs passed by user code. 'Attacker' control therefore means control by the invoking user/peer node, consistent with CWE-78 in a training-cluster setting.

Matching in both extraction queries is syntactic AST-shape matching (Call/Attribute/Subscript patterns). Resolving the callee to the real imported API (e.g. that 'Popen' really is subprocess.Popen) is deferred to LLM labeling, per the Augur candidate strategy.

Predefined distributed-launch functionality (launching the user's training script) is a designed feature and not automatically a vulnerability; the candidate rows preserve receiver/arg-index/shell-mode context so labeling and later triage can make that call.

os.popen/os.system sites with fixed diagnostic strings (role_maker route/ip probing, core.py cpuinfo probing) are kept as candidates; they are expected to be labeled sink/none based on their fixed operands.

The repository root contains audit-looking artifacts (vulnerability_audit_report.md, confirmed_vulns.json, cmd_sinks.csv, patches/). Per experiment constraints these were NOT read; this detection file is based solely on real source code under the repo.
coverage_limits: No 'import subprocess as ...', 'import os as ...' or 'from subprocess import <exec>' aliases exist under python/paddle/ (only 'from subprocess import DEVNULL'), so module-attribute matching on the plain names 'subprocess'/'os' is sufficient; a from-import-verified direct-name branch is included anyway for robustness.
No json/os from-import aliases exist; json.loads/json.load and os.getenv are matched via their module-attribute forms only.
Dynamic dispatch (getattr-based command execution) was searched for and not observed; if a call target cannot be resolved syntactically it will not appear in the candidate set.

paddle.distributed.recv / stream.recv tensor-communication calls also match the '.recv(...)' socket family syntactically; they are emitted as candidates with their receiver expression and are expected to be labeled 'none' for CWE-78 (kept for recall, not pre-filtered).
C++-side command execution in paddle/ (outside the Python database) is out of scope for this Python CodeQL database; only Python-visible bindings such as core.shell_execute_cmd are covered.
